name: Afrobeats
editorial_article: Afrobeats emerged in the 21st century as a distinct West African pop genre, defined by its synthesis of diverse influences such as hip hop, house, jùjú, ndombolo, R&B, soca, and dancehall. While frequently conflated with the 1960s Afrobeat genre pioneered by Fela Kuti, Afrobeats functions as a contemporary, eclectic musical movement separate from the jazz-funk origins of the earlier style. Artists like Mr Eazi, whose journey from tech entrepreneur to stardom was documented in 2017, exemplify the scene's modern, rapid growth. Prominent figures like Tiwa Savage have been highlighted for their contribution to the sound's global reach. Unlike the politically driven, horn-heavy Afrobeat of Africa '70, this current landscape focuses on broader pop-sensibility and rhythmic fusions that bridge the UK and African music scenes.
disambiguator: 2000s–2010s West African pop, distinct from Fela Kuti's Afrobeat
editorial_definition: A 21st-century West African pop genre characterized by an eclectic mix of global influences including hip hop, dancehall, and house, distinct from Fela Kuti's 1960s Afrobeat.
sonic_markers: Eclectic fusion of hip hop, house, highlife, jùjú, and R&B rhythms.
